eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination remains wide open with no formal candidate declarations as of August 2026, producing tight prediction market pricing among Gavin Newsom, Jon Ossoff, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. National polling aggregates show fluctuating leaders such as Kamala Harris or Pete Buttigieg, yet traders assign lower probabilities to them amid questions over electability and party direction after recent cycles. Newsom's early visibility as California governor has drawn scrutiny and some erosion in his market share, while Ossoff has gained ground through Georgia-focused activity and Ossoff's Senate profile. AOC benefits from progressive mobilization in early surveys. The fragmented field, limited recent polling on declared contenders, and uncertainty ahead of the 2026 midterms sustain close odds, with separation likely hinging on future endorsements, primary-state organizing, and performance in emerging national surveys.
